title: Energy balance and dynamic weight-change modelling · Rung 1
subtitle: Why energy balance is arithmetically true and practically insufficient
coverLine: The accounting identity, its units, and why it is not a lever
subject: S01
author: Dr. Harsh Maheshwari

about.why: Every claim about body weight passes, sooner or later, through energy balance. This book teaches the one piece of physics that no argument about obesity is allowed to break: body fat is stored chemical energy, energy is conserved, so fat changes only when what comes in differs from what goes out. It also teaches why that true sentence is not an instruction: intake and expenditure are outputs of a regulated body, not dials you set.
about.howToRead: Read Book 0 first, or at least the sections this book names as it goes. Then read this one in order: each section assumes everything before it. Do every exercise before you read on.

blurb: A short book on the first law of thermodynamics as it applies to a human body: what a kilocalorie is, how large a day of eating, a day of spending and a kilogram of fat are, how to spot a claim that breaks conservation of energy, and why "eat less" does not follow from "energy is conserved".

sections.title: Body fat as stored chemical energy; fat mass and fat-free mass
How much energy a kilogram of body fat holds
A day of intake and a day of expenditure: the sizes
What expenditure is made of, and why a bigger body spends more
The accounting identity for a body
The first law for a body in one sentence, without a lever
Sizing an imbalance, and the static rule
Spotting a claim that breaks conservation
Intake and expenditure are outputs of a regulated system
